name: Bandhan Bank Ltd
title: Bandhan Bank Ltd - 541153 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Bandhan Q4FY26 shows EEB stress easing: slippages fell to INR 1,028 crore from 1,314 crore and credit cost 2% vs 3.3%, with NIM up to 6.2%, but ROA of 1.1% is still far from the 1.6-1.7% exit-FY27 target.

summary.headline: Bandhan Bank Q4FY26 PAT rose 68% YoY to INR 534 crore, with NIM up to 6.2% and credit cost easing to 2%.
summary.overview: Bandhan Bank reported Q4FY26 PAT of INR 534 crore, up 68% YoY and 159% QoQ, with ROA of 1.1% and ROE of 9% for the quarter. NIM rose to 6.2% from 5.9% in Q3 on a 23 bps QoQ fall in deposit costs, while credit cost fell to 2% from 3.3%. Slippages declined to INR 1,028 crore from INR 1,314 crore, led by EEB, and collection efficiency improved. Full-year FY26 PAT was INR 1,224 crore, with NII down 5.8% YoY, and opex was elevated in Q4 by PSLC and IT items.

financial_highlights.change: from 31% last year; bulk deposits -7% YoY

segments.name: EEB (microfinance and related)
segments.commentary: EEB book INR 53,906 crore, down YoY (about -5%) but up 8% QoQ; 23% of advances. EEB slippages fell to INR 690 crore from INR 942 crore; 0-90 DPD pool fell to about 3.1% from 4.6%.

segments.name: Non-EEB book
segments.commentary: Non-EEB advances grew 25% YoY and form about two-thirds of total advances. Retail grew 46% YoY (CV, CE, auto, gold loans); wholesale grew 33% YoY.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book grew 25% YoY and forms about 56% of advances, against a target of 58% by March 2027.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Other income grew 10% YoY and 12% QoQ; third-party distribution income rose 34% YoY and processing fees rebounded.

guidance_outlook: ROA guided at 1.6%-1.7% (management also cited 1.6%-1.8%, give or take 10 bps) by exit FY27 (Q4FY27); management says it will work towards this, calling it a challenge.
NIM guided at around 6% on total assets (about 6.5% on earning assets) by exit FY27; a further 10-20 bps improvement expected over the next 2-3 quarters from term deposit repricing.
Credit cost guided at 1.6%-1.7% by Q4FY27 from 2% in Q4FY26; FY26 credit cost was 3%.
Advances growth targeted at around 14%-15%; deposit growth to be better than advances, but industry credit growth now exceeds deposit growth.
PSL certificate cost expected to fall about 50% in FY27 versus FY26 and to be nearly neutralised in FY28.
Opex-to-average-assets remains a focus; FY26 was about 4% against guidance. Other income to add about 10 bps to ROA.

Expected ECL transition impact about INR 1,250 crore (based on December 2025 portfolio), spread over 5 years at about INR 250 crore a year, or roughly 16-17 bps CRAR impact each year; flow impact still being computed under the latest circular.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 1,955 branches; housing finance centres largely upgraded to full banking branches, some merged with existing branches.
4,400 EEB banking units across the country.
Average LCR in Q4 ranged 130%-140%; period-end LCR about 131%, down from about 200% a year earlier as bulk deposits fell.
Capital adequacy 18.0% CRAR and 17.3% Tier 1; management says ample headroom for growth.
demand_pricing: Collection efficiency ex-NPA improved to 98.9% in March 2026 from 98.1% in December 2025; EEB quarter-wide efficiency 99.3% vs 98.2% in Q3.

Collection efficiency ex-bucket 99.6% for Q4 (99.3% in Q3) and 99.7% for March; management says no adverse effect on collections from elections or the Middle East war so far in April, though a few basis points dipped.
Deposit competition is intense; competitor deposit rates rose sharply in March 2026, and bank chose not to grow bulk deposits in Q4.
Yield on advances rose 14 bps QoQ, helped by the Q3 ARC sale removing NPAs from the base and the EEB mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 4% QoQ despite strong advance growth and margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the back-ended loan growth (about 50% of incremental FY growth came in Q4, with late-March disbursals not yet earning), two fewer days in the quarter, and the 25 bps December repo cut impacting about 46% of the book (11 bps effect).

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state credit cost after the RBI ECL norms, and what are the standard asset provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds about INR 1,072 crore of standard asset provisions, including an extra 75 bps on standard assets: EEB at 1% vs 0.25% required, and personal loans/ABG at about 0.4%. Flow impact is still being computed; the INR 1,250 crore transition estimate is based on the December 2025 book.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins keep improving, and what is the NIM trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects another 10-20 bps of NIM improvement over the next 2-3 quarters as term deposits reprice, with a best-effort aim of about 6% NIM on total assets by exit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the PSL shortfall and how will it be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 PSLC cost was about INR 150 crore (INR 60 crore higher QoQ). The aim is a roughly 50% cut in FY27 and near zero in FY28, with EEB loans qualifying for PSL rising from about 10-15% to about 40%, targeting 60-65%.

qa_highlights.question: What were the one-off items in opex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 120 crore in recurring-type items: PSLC cost up around INR 60 crore QoQ and IT expenses up around INR 50 crore, with timing-related elements expected not to repeat immediately. Separately, INR 73 crore extra employee cost came from keeping branches open on holidays.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a government deposit share and how much is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Government deposits are about INR 6,000 crore; about 12% of CASA is from government deposits. Retail composition, including CASA and retail term deposits, rose to 74% from 69% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA path and what would drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA rose from 0.2% in September to 0.4% in December and 1.1% in Q4. Drivers cited are lower credit cost, higher NIM, higher other income (about 10 bps expected), and lower PSLC costs; management acknowledged a 50-60 bps journey to the target.

risks_watch: Middle East war and fuel price or availability effects on the economy and collections; management has not quantified the impact.
ECL transition: about INR 1,250 crore (based on December 2025 data), with flow impact still to be computed under the latest RBI circular; the choice between P&L and reserves is pending.
Deposit cost pressure from intense competition; more term deposit renewals are due over the next 2-3 quarters.
Credit growth (about 14%-15% target) is running ahead of deposit growth across the industry; the bank has not added bulk deposits.
Non-recurring PSLC and IT costs; opex-to-assets was 4.4% in Q4 against about 4% for FY26.
Vishal Wadhwa (EEB head) resigned, citing personal career advancement; management says the process is now process-driven.
Management stated no NPA sale is currently planned, but an ARC-sale option remains open.
Media reports of promoter-level activity; management called them rumours and said there is no impact on the Bank's shareholding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's momentum (margins, slippages, collections) but cautious on the Middle East war, deposit competition and the ECL transition, which management said it is still assessing. Answers on ROA and credit cost were direct but qualified as "a challenge" and "best effort". Some answers on the NIM and fee targets were less specific.
key_quotes: The EEB segment has not only stabilized but also delivered good sequential growth, reinforcing our confidence in the portfolio.
So, the slippages have been most, last quarter, it was INR 1,314 crores, it has come down to INR 1028 in Q4.
Definitely, a challenge, but we are not changing the guidance as of now.
So, our guidance, we have mentioned was between 1.6% to 1.7% by the exit of FY27, which is by Q4FY27. And we will still endeavour to work towards that.
I think the deposit competition is definitely intense, and we did see in the month of March itself, the deposit rates go up quite significantly being offered by the competition.

growth.why: Management targets advances growth of 14%-15% in FY27 and ROA of 1.6%-1.7% by Q4FY27, with credit cost falling to 1.6%-1.7% and NIM rising 10-20 bps over 2-3 quarters; backing is partial (secured mix toward 58%, PSL cost down ~50%, collections improving) with no specific new capacity or order numbers, and the branch network is described without expansion plans.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: next 2-3 quarters; ROA 1.6%-1.7% by Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management guides at least another 10-20 bps NIM improvement over 2-3 quarters from term deposit repricing (NIM 6.2% in Q4 FY26, target about 6% on total assets by exit FY27), credit cost falling from 2% to 1.6%-1.7%, and PSL cost down about 50% in FY27; ROA is only 1.1% in Q4 against a 1.6%-1.7% target, a 50-60 bps journey.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network held at 1,955 with housing finance centres merged into existing branches and 4,400 EEB banking units; no new branch or capacity expansion plans were stated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances growth targeted at 14%-15% in FY27 from gross advances of INR 1.54 lakh crore (+13% YoY), with non-EEB book up 25% YoY and retail up 46% YoY; deposits of INR 1.66 lakh crore (+10% YoY) need to keep pace, though bulk deposits fell 7% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: CRAR is 18.0% with ample headroom per management and no capex or land plans were discussed, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding guidance (ROA 1.6%-1.7%, credit cost 1.6%-1.7%, advances 14%-15%) and calls the ROA target a challenge at 1.1% in Q4 against a 1.6%-1.7% goal, with ECL transition impact of about INR 1,250 crore still being computed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ECL transition of about INR 1,250 crore (16-17 bps CRAR per year over 5 years) and flow impact still pending, Middle East war effects unquantified, and deposit competition with more term deposit renewals due, against an ROA target of 1.6%-1.7% from 1.1% today.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed.

rows.label: PSL certificate cost cut about 50% in FY27
rows.why: Q4 PSLC cost was about INR 150 crore (INR 60 crore higher QoQ), and EEB loans qualifying for PSL are to rise from about 10-15% to about 40%, targeting 60-65%.

rows.label: CASA ratio rebuild and bulk deposit runoff
rows.why: CASA rose to INR 48,752 crore (29.3% of deposits, up about 200 bps QoQ) while bulk deposits fell to about 26% from 31%, but LCR of about 131% is down from about 200% a year earlier and deposit competition is intense.

rows.label: Term deposit repricing lifts NIM
rows.why: NIM rose to 6.2% from 5.9% as deposit costs fell 23 bps QoQ, with more term deposit renewals due and management expecting at least another 10-20 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 momentum (NIM 6.2%, credit cost 2%, collections 99.6%) but cautious on the Middle East war, deposit competition and the ECL transition; analysts pushed on the NII only 4% QoQ rise, the ROA path from 1.1% to 1.6%-1.7%, and the one-off PSLC and IT opex.
